etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English superfluous, from Latin superfluus (“superfluous”) + -ous, from superfluō (“overflow”), from super (“above, more than, over”) + fluō (“flow”). Compare mellifluous and fluid, also from Latin. Literally corresponds to overflow, which is from Germanic, rather than Latin. By surface analysis, super- +‎ -fluous.
senses: In excess of what is required or sufficient.
